import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 660

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/660](https://www.erdosproblems.com/660)
- [Er97e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite problems and results*, The mathematics of Paul Erdős,
  I (1997), 47–67.
- [Al63] Altman, E., *On a problem of P. Erdős*, Amer. Math. Monthly (1963), 148–157.
- [Er75f] Erdős, Paul, *On some problems of elementary and combinatorial geometry*, Ann. Mat. Pura
  Appl. (4) (1975), 99–108.
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace Erdos660

/--
`P` is the set of vertices of a (full-dimensional) convex polyhedron in $\mathbb{R}^3$: the points
are in convex position and they affinely span $\mathbb{R}^3$ (so the polyhedron is genuinely
three-dimensional).
-/
def IsPolyhedronVertices (P : Finset ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ConvexIndependent ℝ ((↑) : ↥(P : Set ℝ³) → ℝ³) ∧ affineSpan ℝ (P : Set ℝ³) = ⊤

/--
Let $x_1, \ldots, x_n \in \mathbb{R}^3$ be the vertices of a convex polyhedron. Are there at least
$$(1 - o(1)) \frac{n}{2}$$
many distinct distances between the $x_i$?

The $(1 - o(1)) \frac{n}{2}$ lower bound is formalised as: for every $\varepsilon > 0$, every set
of $n$ vertices of a convex polyhedron with $n$ sufficiently large determines at least
$(1 - \varepsilon) \frac{n}{2}$ distinct distances.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 52]
theorem erdos_660 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, ∀ P : Finset ℝ³,
        P.card = n → IsPolyhedronVertices P →
        (1 - ε) * ((n : ℝ) / 2) ≤ (distinctDistances P : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
For the similar problem in $\mathbb{R}^2$ there are always at least $n/2$ distances, as proved by
Altman [Al63].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 51 52]
theorem erdos_660.variants.altman_planar (n : ℕ) (P : Finset ℝ²)
    (hcard : P.card = n) (hconv : ConvexIndependent ℝ ((↑) : ↥(P : Set ℝ²) → ℝ²))
    (haff : affineSpan ℝ (P : Set ℝ²) = ⊤) :
    n / 2 ≤ distinctDistances P := by
  sorry

/--
In [Er75f] Erdős claims that Altman proved that the vertices determine $\gg n$ many distinct
distances, but gives no reference.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 52]
theorem erdos_660.variants.Er75f :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, ∀ P : Finset ℝ³,
      P.card = n → IsPolyhedronVertices P →
      c * n ≤ (distinctDistances P : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos660

findings.description: The bibliography entry labelled [Er97e] (lines 24–25) has the wrong title, publication, and page range. It lists “Some of my favorite problems and results”, The mathematics of Paul Erdős I, 47–67, rather than the reference used for problem 660. This does not affect the Lean statements.
findings.source_evidence: https://erdosproblems.com/660 cites [Er97e, p.531]. https://erdosproblems.com/bibs/Er97e identifies it as Erdős, Paul, “Some of my favourite unsolved problems”, Math. Japon. (1997), 527–537.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the [Er97e] entry with the correct title, journal, and pages; the relevant passage is on p.531.

findings.description: The docstring says “at least n/2 distances”, whereas the correct bound, and the bound actually stated in Lean using natural-number division, is floor(n/2). The distinction matters for odd n: an equilateral triangle has three vertices but only one distinct distance. The theorem itself is correctly formalized.
findings.source_evidence: The linked planar problem, https://erdosproblems.com/latex/93, explicitly states “at least floor(n/2) distinct distances” and attributes this to Altman [Al63]. Erdős’s [Er75f], p.100 (https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1975-25.pdf), likewise gives the integer-part bound, with equality for regular polygons. The abbreviated wording on page 660 omits this rounding.
findings.suggested_fix: Change only the docstring to say “at least $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ distances”. Keep the natural-number inequality in the theorem unchanged.

reformulations.difference: Lean expresses Altman’s floor bound through natural-number division rather than an explicit floor of a real quotient.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every natural n, Nat.floor ((n : ℝ) / 2) = n / 2. Consequently the Lean inequality is precisely the floor(n/2) bound in problem 93 and [Er75f], not a weaker approximation to Altman’s theorem. The corresponding inequality equivalence was proved in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: The declaration asks for a non-strict linear lower bound only for sufficiently large n, while the 1975 passage states a positive linear bound without that restriction.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every admissible vertex set has at least four points and at least one distinct distance. Given c > 0 and a threshold N for the Lean bound, choose c' = min(c/2, 1/(N+1)). For n ≥ N, c'n < cn ≤ D; for n < N, c'n < 1 ≤ D. Thus a positive strict linear bound holds for every admissible set. The converse is immediate. This full equivalence, including the geometric cardinality and distance-positivity facts, was proved in Lean without using the problem theorems.

review.notes: All four declarations were checked; no mathematical statement defect was found. The main theorem matches the source site’s corrected lower-bound formulation. The source discussion acknowledges ambiguity in Erdős’s original wording and explicitly adopts this interpretation, so the historical wording is not a defect in this file. The source still records the main problem as open and treats the three-dimensional Altman attribution as an unreferenced historical claim; no definite status correction is warranted. Scratch checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compile successfully and verify distance-counting semantics, empty/singleton cases, minimum admissible cardinalities, the uniform threshold quantifiers, the equilateral-triangle distance count, and the recorded equivalences. The original full texts of [Al63] and [Er97e] were not retrieved directly; their relevant statements were checked through problem 93, the source’s quotation of [Er97e], and the accessible primary [Er75f] paper. The reviewed file was not modified.
